clue.text: Spooner's to overfill seaman's transport

indicators.note: Spooner's version means the opening sounds of two words are swapped, as the Reverend Spooner was said to do

blocks.note: to overfill is to cram and a seaman is a tar; swap their opening sounds

explanation.surface: A sailor's way of getting about, described as something that overfills.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of CRAM TAR and you get TRAM CAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramcar is a passenger vehicle on rails, a form of public transport.

clue.text: Confusion no good in narrative

indicators.note: in places the first part inside the story that follows it

blocks.note: a tale is a story
N for no and G for good, both standard abbreviations

explanation.surface: A story that is no good is just a muddle.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangle is a twisted, muddled state, so it is a synonym for confusion.

clue.text: Esoteric artist put up with punishment when young

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means written from bottom to top, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: RA is a Royal Academician, the crossword artist
the cane was once a schoolchild's punishment

explanation.surface: An obscure painter remembers being caned as a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric and arcane are synonyms, both meaning understood only by a few initiates.

clue.text: Miner's daughter providing fruit

blocks.note: first meaning: the heroine of the folk song Oh My Darling, whose father was a forty-niner miner
second meaning: a small citrus fruit like a mandarin

explanation.surface: A mining family's girl hands out fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The American folk song 'Oh My Darling, Clementine' tells of a miner's daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to the song's heroine and to a small seedless orange-like citrus.

clue.text: Old Italian soldiers turned up on island

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means flipped to run bottom to top, so the letters go backwards

blocks.note: OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers
the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: Ancient Italian troops arriving on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman was a citizen of ancient Rome, so an Italian of old times.

clue.text: Theatrical base where you're prone to take it easy?

definitions.text: where you're prone to take it easy?

blocks.note: camp means exaggerated and showy
a bed is a foundation, as in a riverbed

explanation.surface: A stage setting where one lies down and relaxes.
explanation.walkthrough: Prone means lying face down, but it also hints at being inclined to laze.
explanation.definitionFit: A camp bed is a folding bed you lie flat on to rest, so prone is literal.

clue.text: Stop a lobby rising in California ahead of time

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means reading upward, so the letters run backwards
in puts the reversed phrase inside the state abbreviation
ahead of places the boxed group before the final letter

blocks.note: a hall is an entrance lobby
Cal is a standard abbreviation for California
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A lobby group in California is rising up against something.
explanation.definitionFit: To call a halt is an idiom for ordering something to stop.

clue.text: Skimpy skirt attendant can't get on

indicators.note: can't get on is read as being unable to keep the letters spelling on, so they drop out

blocks.note: a minion is a servile follower or attendant

explanation.surface: An assistant cannot squeeze into a very short skirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A mini is a very short skirt, the miniskirt, hence skimpy.

clue.text: Nudity unusually seen in pubs

indicators.note: unusually means in an odd way, so these letters are rearranged
in places the jumbled letters inside the drinking places

blocks.note: the letters of seen rearranged
bars are pubs

explanation.surface: Naked people are rarely spotted in pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Bareness is the state of being uncovered, a synonym for nudity.

clue.text: Honourable combatant expected on s-schedule

blocks.note: due means expected, as a train is due
the stammered s-s tells you to stammer the synonym too: list becomes l-list

explanation.surface: A fighter of honour is due to appear on a schedule, stammered nervously.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutter in s-schedule is copied onto its synonym list, doubling its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A duellist fights a formal duel to settle a point of honour.

clue.text: Corner provincial revolutionary?

blocks.note: Northern Ireland is called the Province, abbreviated NI
Che Guevara, the Argentine-born revolutionary

explanation.surface: A question asking whether a rebel from the provinces can be cornered.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a recess or nook, a small corner set into a wall.

clue.text: Hospital employee who takes care of post, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says a word is to be taken by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: post is mail, which sounds like the word for a man
a nurse is someone who tends and cares for others

explanation.surface: A hospital worker who looks after the post.
explanation.definitionFit: A male nurse is a man employed on hospital wards to care for patients.

clue.text: Strong feature that makes the face light up?

definitions.text: Strong feature that makes the face light up?

blocks.note: surface reading: a prominent facial feature
setter's reading: a face that lights up like a lamp, punning on the lamp in the name

explanation.walkthrough: Light up suggests a happy smile, but read literally it points to a lamp that illuminates.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, protruding lower jaw is named after the shape of an old lamp, a strong facial feature.

clue.text: Endless row over nothing

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its final letter
over means turned over, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: a row is a line

explanation.surface: An argument that never ends, about nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Row suggests a quarrel, but here it is a line of things.
explanation.definitionFit: Nil means zero, nothing at all, as in a football score.

clue.text: Peculiar characters appearing on right-hand pages?

definitions.note: describes the answer rather than naming it: the numbers found on right-hand pages

blocks.note: odd means strange
numbers are written characters, numerals

explanation.surface: Strange people turning up on certain pages.
explanation.walkthrough: Characters suggests people, but numerals are characters too.
explanation.definitionFit: In books the right-hand page, the recto, conventionally carries an odd page number.

clue.text: Isn't sadder as lunatic keeps uniform

indicators.note: lunatic means crazy, so the preceding letters are scrambled

blocks.note: the letters of these three words, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A madman claims he is no sadder while dressed the same as everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: To standardise is to make things conform to one standard, keeping them uniform.

clue.text: Cool novel Verne's written about the French

indicators.note: novel means new, so the author's name is given a new arrangement
written about means set down around something, so it encloses what follows

blocks.note: the letters of Verne's rearranged
les is French for the, plural

explanation.surface: A fine novel by Jules Verne about the French.
explanation.walkthrough: Novel looks like a book by Verne, but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerveless can mean calm and composed under pressure, so it means cool.

clue.text: Cook callin' by to get cooking pot

indicators.note: to cook something is to fiddle with it, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A cook drops by to borrow a pan.
explanation.definitionFit: A billycan is a metal pot used for cooking or boiling water over a campfire.

clue.text: Son having best parts removed yelled in anguish

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
to cream off is to take the best part away

explanation.surface: A boy cried out in pain when his best bits were taken away.
explanation.definitionFit: Screamed means cried out loudly, as one does in pain or anguish.

clue.text: Popular type of film, with rocket going up in smoke

blocks.note: in means fashionable
cine film is the film used in old home movie cameras
a rocket is a severe telling-off, and so is a rating

explanation.surface: A popular film with a rocket launch exploding in flames.
explanation.walkthrough: Rocket looks like a firework, but in British slang a rocket is a scolding, and to rate someone is to scold them.
explanation.definitionFit: Incinerating means burning something to ashes, so it is literally going up in smoke.

clue.text: Ancient ruler's reportedly a grasper

indicators.note: reportedly means as told by word of mouth, so the sound counts, not the spelling

blocks.note: one who grasps is a seizer

explanation.surface: An ancient emperor described as greedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar was the title of Roman emperors, rulers of the ancient world.

clue.text: Skilled lovers, educated to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent means only part of the following words is used

blocks.note: found running across the two words

explanation.surface: Expert lovers who have been taught to a degree.
explanation.definitionFit: To be versed in something is to be experienced and knowledgeable, hence skilled.

clue.text: Deceit admitted by client

indicators.note: admitted by means let inside, so the answer sits within the next word

blocks.note: the middle letters of this word

explanation.surface: A customer confesses to having deceived someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A lie is a deliberate falsehood, an act of deceit.

clue.text: Radio range picked up by spiritualist?

definitions.text: Radio range picked up by spiritualist?

blocks.note: surface reading: a band of broadcast frequencies
setter's reading: a signal a psychic might receive from beyond

explanation.walkthrough: A spiritualist who contacts the dead is also called a medium, and picking up suggests receiving a transmission.
explanation.definitionFit: Medium wave is the band of radio frequencies used for AM broadcasting.

clue.text: Problem children

blocks.note: first meaning: a matter in dispute
second meaning: offspring, in legal language

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as problem children; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue means both a point of contention and one's descendants, as in died without issue.

clue.text: Posh car loses second wheel

indicators.note: loses means a letter is taken away from the car's name

blocks.note: a Rolls-Royce, a luxury car
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: An expensive car has lost one of its wheels.
explanation.walkthrough: Wheel is a verb here, not the car part.
explanation.definitionFit: To roll and to wheel both mean to turn over and over or move on wheels.

clue.text: Plain folk, those arriving around beginning of week

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the arrivals wrap round the day's start

blocks.note: comers are people who come
Mon is the abbreviation for Monday, the start of the week

explanation.surface: Ordinary people arriving at the start of the week.
explanation.definitionFit: Commoners are people without noble rank, ordinary folk.

clue.text: Is more relaxed when there's no time for kids

indicators.note: no means without, so the time letter is removed

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
to kid someone is to tease them

explanation.surface: A parent relaxes when there is no time to spend with the children.
explanation.walkthrough: Kids looks like children, but it is a verb meaning jokes with.
explanation.definitionFit: If something eases, it slackens or becomes less tense, so it is more relaxed.

clue.text: Learner undoes loose knots, small ones

indicators.note: loose means set free from order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: L is the learner plate
taken as written

explanation.surface: A learner unties loose little knots.
explanation.definitionFit: A nodule is a small rounded lump or knot, as in wood or tissue.

clue.text: Survived with son, not daughter, safely delivered

definitions.note: ensured is past tense, as delivered is a participle

indicators.note: son is put in place of daughter, so one abbreviation replaces the other

blocks.note: to endure is to last or survive
S is the abbreviation for son
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A mother survived the birth of a son, not a daughter, safely.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensure is to make certain of something, so ensured means guaranteed or secured.
